plot: At Peterborough Abbey in 1127 a Murk Crow and a night watchman tell Odo what the Peterborough Chronicle recorded after greedy Abbot Henry of Poitou arrived: black huntsmen on black horses and goats, wide-eyed hounds, horns every night until Easter — and the hunt circles Odo's lantern.

script.title: Never Look Up When the Black Hunt Rides By

beats.say: This is a true record. In the year eleven twenty-seven, English monks wrote down what rode past their abbey at night.
The place was Peterborough. The book is the Peterborough Chronicle, kept by the monks of its abbey.
Peterborough. Peterborough. Who walks to the abbey so late?
Just me. And my lantern. Who are you?
I repeat what people whisper. And the monks whispered a great deal that winter.
That winter, the abbey was given a new abbot. His name was Henry of Poitou.
The chronicle says he stripped the abbey of its wealth and sent it overseas.
Our chronicle says he lived like a drone in a beehive. Taking. Never giving.
And then what happened?
He came to us in early February. And soon after, the hunting began.
The chronicle says many men both saw and heard huntsmen, hunting in the dark.
The huntsmen were black, and big, and loathsome. They rode on black horses, and on black goats.
And their hounds were all black, with wide, staring eyes.
Goats? They were riding goats?
Black goats. Black goats. That's what they wrote.
They were seen in the abbey's own deer park, and in all the woods from Peterborough to Stamford.
Our watchmen kept guard through the night. They reckoned twenty, perhaps thirty horn-blowers.
Thirty riders... and nobody stopped them?
Nobody could. We monks heard the horns at night, all through Lent, right up to Easter.
Shh. Shh. Do you hear it, lantern boy?
Something is running between the trees!
Across Europe, people told of a Wild Hunt: ghostly riders and hounds racing through winter nights.
To meet it, the old tales said, was a warning. Something in the world had gone wrong.
So the monks believed the hunt came because of the abbot?
We wrote what we saw and heard. You may judge the rest.
Wrong. Wrong. And the abbot? Ask what became of him.
The chronicler ends with a bitter line. Of his going, he wrote, we cannot yet say.
Years later, Henry was removed from Peterborough. The riders were never explained.
Then they could still be out there.
Keep your lantern high, child. Hunters do not like to be seen.
They see you, lantern boy. They see you.
Don't look up. Don't look up...
Nearly nine hundred years later, the monks' words survive, in the pages of their chronicle.
Read them on a cold February night, and see if you can stop listening for horns.

long.title: Never Look Up When the Black Hunt Rides By 🐺
long.description:
A true record from 1127: after a greedy new abbot reached Peterborough, the monks' own chronicle tells of black huntsmen on black horses and goats, wide-eyed hounds, and horns blowing every night until Easter. Was it a warning — or something else? Tell us what you think.

Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_of_Poitou · strangehistory.net/2018/01/28/wild-hunt-1127/

#truestory #wildhunt #folklore

es.title: Nunca mires arriba cuando pasa la Cacería Negra 🐺
es.description:
Un registro real de 1127: tras la llegada de un abad codicioso a Peterborough, la crónica de los monjes habla de cazadores negros sobre caballos y cabras negras, perros de ojos enormes y cuernos cada noche hasta Pascua. ¿Fue una advertencia? Cuéntanos qué piensas.

Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_of_Poitou · strangehistory.net/2018/01/28/wild-hunt-1127/

#historiareal #caceriasalvaje #folclore

Um registro real de 1127: depois que um abade ganancioso chegou a Peterborough, a crônica dos monges fala de caçadores negros em cavalos e bodes negros, cães de olhos arregalados e trompas toda noite até a Páscoa. Foi um aviso? Diga o que você acha.

fr.title: Ne levez jamais les yeux quand passe la Chasse Noire 🐺
fr.description:
Un récit réel de 1127 : après l'arrivée d'un abbé avide à Peterborough, la chronique des moines décrit des chasseurs noirs sur des chevaux et des boucs noirs, des chiens aux yeux écarquillés et des cors chaque nuit jusqu'à Pâques. Un avertissement ? Dites-nous ce que vous en pensez.

#histoirevraie #chassesauvage #folklore

ja.title: 黒い狩りが通る時、決して見上げるな 🐺
ja.description:
1127年の実際の記録。強欲な新修道院長がピーターバラに来た後、修道士の年代記は、黒い馬と黒いヤギに乗った黒い狩人、目を見開いた猟犬、そして復活祭まで毎晩響く角笛を記しました。それは警告だったのか?あなたの考えを教えてください。
